resources.string: Tap to adjust. Mochi naps while there is nothing to show.
A little island for your camera
Brings back anything swiped away and checks music, notifications and devices again.
Copies the lines above, handy for a bug report.
Mochi has no internet permission, so nothing leaves your phone.
Its accessibility service asks for no screen access. It is only used to sit above the status bar.

string-array.name: whats_new_notes
string-array.item: Expanding no longer slides the card\'s content sideways. A swiped-away pill comes back. Island status in About.
Steadier overlay window and shade handling.
Tap Mochi\'s face and it winks.
Mochi taps Quick Settings tile for payment apps.
Accessibility no longer asks to read the screen.
Animated icons for downloads, uploads, extracting and compressing.
New name, Material 3 Expressive design and Material You colours.

resources.string: Mochi is awake and sitting on your camera.
Mochi is asleep. Turn it on to wake it up.
Finish setup below so Mochi can wake up.

Recommended. Puts Mochi above the status bar so taps, media buttons and swipes work. Mochi asks for no screen access, so it can\'t read anything you see. If the switch is greyed out: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings. If a payment app still refuses to open, turn this off while you pay. Mochi keeps showing; only taps pause.
Fallback when accessibility is off. Mochi shows, but the status bar takes the taps.
Needed for music, notifications and live activities.
Needed to read the name and battery of your earbuds.
Android 13+ needs this for the tiny background notice.
Stops your phone from putting Mochi to sleep in the background.
To switch taps on from the tile, run the one-time command shown in Mochi\'s Setup. For now, turn Mochi on here.
Ready. Add the Mochi taps tile to turn taps off before a payment app and back on after. The island keeps showing either way.
Turns taps off before a payment app and back on after, in one tap. Turning them back on needs a one-time command from a computer: tap Copy, then run it with adb while your phone is connected.
Command copied. Run it with adb, then come back.
Edit your Quick Settings panel and drag Mochi taps in.
Shows Mochi above the status bar so you can tap it.

Mochi uses accessibility only to draw the island above the status bar, so it can be tapped, and to notice when the notification shade or lock screen comes to the front so it can hide. It requests no access to screen content, so it cannot read what is on your screen, and it has no internet access.
Turn on Accessibility or Display over other apps first.
Not normally needed. Auto reads the camera from Android and re-fits after rotation or display changes.
Android reports a camera at the top %1$s: %2$d × %3$d dp, from the %4$s. Mochi is sized around it and centred on it.
Android reports no camera at the top of the screen right now, for example in landscape. Mochi floats at the top centre.
Centre is chosen. Choose Auto to wrap the camera.

Android reports a %1$d × %2$d dp box in the top %3$s corner. A camera never touches the screen edge, so that box is padding and the hole is estimated inside it. Tap Line up with camera for an exact fit.
Using your line-up: a %1$d dp camera at the top %2$s.

Drag anywhere to move the ring onto the black camera hole, then pinch or use the slider until it just fits around it. The arrows move it 1 px; hold for 5 px. The dashed outline is where Mochi will sit.
Animated music bars in the pill
Haptic tick when Mochi pops up
Show live activities (stopwatch, timer, calls, downloads, uploads, compressing, navigation)
Hide while the notification shade or lock screen is open
Taps only work with Accessibility on. Without it the status bar takes the taps.

Some phones close background apps aggressively. For Mochi to stay around:

• App info → Battery usage → Allow background activity
• App info → Auto-launch → on
• Settings → Battery → App battery management → Mochi → Don't optimise
• In recents, swipe down on Mochi's card and tap Lock
